summary: GKE CI runners failing to reprovision SSH keys after node-pool rotation during secret-rotation window
description:
Issue summary:
During the scheduled secret rotation for the CI runner fleet (node pool autoscale + instance reprovisioning) a subset of GKE nodes came up without the runner SSH bootstrap keys. Affected CI jobs report: 'ssh: handshake failed' and the runner pod cannot be reached for job startup.

Impact:
- ~15% of release CI jobs in prod-us-east failing to acquire runners, causing release queue stalls and blocked deploys for multiple teams (release engineering, serving-runtime).
- Ticket flagged P1 / Sev1 due to release impact and increased manual intervention.

Environment:
- GKE autopilot-managed node pools (node-pool-release-2026a) in prod-us-east
- Runners are created as NodePools auto-provisioned; SSH keys are normally bootstrapped via node-init DaemonSet that reads from KMS-backed secrets in Vault and writes instance metadata for the runner user.
- Secret rotation window: 2026-03-10 02:00-03:00 UTC

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Triggered rotation: infra job rotated vault secret consumer role (vault-role-runner) and rolled GKE node-pool by cordon/drain + recreate.
2) New nodes booted but the node-init logs show failures to call metadata server to set instance-level SSH key metadata: "403 Forbidden: Permission denied to write metadata".
3) Runner provisioning waits for SSH connectivity; retries time out.

Relevant logs/snippets:
- node-init pod (node-init-7f8f): /var/log/node-init.log: "error: metadata write failed: googleapi: Error 403: The caller does not have permission"
- kubelet event on new node: "node.kubernetes.io/unreachable: Node lost contact with control plane for > 60s" (transient)
- CI controller: "failed to allocate runner: ssh handshake error: unable to authenticate"

Hypothesis / initial theory:
- The Vault role rotation changed the GCP service account key used by node-init; node-init switched to a short-lived token that cannot write instance metadata because the instance's service-account-scopes or IAM binding lacks compute.instances.setMetadata permission. Alternatively, the rotation temporarily removed the impersonation binding between the infra service account and the GKE node SA, causing metadata writes to 403.

Immediate workaround attempted:
- Manually restarted node-init DaemonSet on affected nodes (kubectl rollout restart ds/node-init) — intermittent success: some nodes picked up keys afterward.
- Temporarily reverted Vault consumer role to previous version to allow nodes with older credentials to bootstrap (mitigated ~70% failures).

Current blockers:
- Can't fully reproduce in staging because autopilot behavior differs for instance metadata access control.
- Lack of a safe long-lived credential that node-init can use during secret rotation windows without escalating risk.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 03:15: Support slack #infra: Raised incident to release engineering. Posted logs and node-init errors.

Checked IAM bindings for infra-runner-impersonator@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com — found missing compute.instances.setMetadata on the impersonated node service account after role rotation (diff in audit log: GRANT removed at 2026-03-10T02:05Z).
Examined Vault audit: the role role-runner-consumer had a policy update during rotation which removed 'gcp/iam/token/impersonate' for node-init service account, likely causing token scope reduction.
Recreated a test node via gcloud and validated that a token without 'setMetadata' permission results in the same 403 from the metadata API endpoint.
CI controller's retry backoff caused queue growth; temporary manual job requeue was used as a stopgap for blocking releases.
comments: Aisha Mehta (Reporter) - 2026-03-10: Noticed surge in 'ssh handshake' errors starting 02:13 UTC during rotation window. Opening ticket so infra can investigate IAM drift during rotation.
Diego Ramirez (Assignee) - 2026-03-10: Investigating IAM audit logs and Vault role change. I've isolated a missing impersonation grant; working on a safe remediation plan. Will update in 30m.

SRE Team (Slack #infra) - 2026-03-10: Suggested manual reapply of compute.instances.setMetadata on node SA as short term fix. Coordinating with cloud-admins to perform changes during low-traffic minutes.
Release Eng (Slack) - 2026-03-10: We had 6 release jobs blocked; manual requeues allowed two of them to complete. Please prioritize; new deploys are queued.

Diego Ramirez - 2026-03-11: Applied IAM binding regrant to node SA and re-rolled node-init DaemonSet. New nodes now successfully write metadata on bootstrap in canary group (5/5 success). Rolling to remaining nodes over next maintenance window.
Security (Emily Zhao) - 2026-03-11: Concern raised about long-lived credentials. Recommend a vault rekey + limited-time bootstrap token. Follow-up action item created.

Diego Ramirez - 2026-03-12: Implemented canary rollout and added an automated post-rotation healthcheck that verifies node-init metadata writes. Queue length returned to normal. Leaving ticket open for follow-up items.
resolution:
Partial remediation applied: Re-applied compute.instances.setMetadata IAM binding to the GKE node service account and re-deployed node-init DaemonSet. Canaried on 5 nodes (all healthy) and then rolled to remaining nodes — observed successful SSH key bootstrap across the fleet.

Permanent fix plan (follow-ups):
- Create a short-lived bootstrap credential flow: generate time-limited GCP tokens via Vault that include explicit metadata write scope and are automatically revoked post-bootstrap. (Owner: infra-team, due 2026-04-02)
- Update the secret-rotation runbook to include preflight IAM-binding verification and a pre-rotation canary on a staging node pool. (Owner: release-engineering-docs, due 2026-03-20)
- Add an automated post-rotation healthcheck that validates SSH connectivity and node-init log for 'metadata write success' (done as interim; extend to alerting). (Owner: Diego Ramirez, done 2026-03-12)

Status: In Progress — immediate release impact mitigated, follow-up tickets created for permanent solution.
next_steps: Create INT follow-up: implement Vault-to-GCP short-lived bootstrap flow (INT-13045)
Add pre-rotation IAM verification step in automation (owner: infra/automation)
Schedule runbook workshop with security to validate acceptable token TTLs for bootstrap use
